newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS MASTERFUL IN BLUE JAYS DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS MASTERFUL IN BLUE JAYS DEBUT.

text.p: Roger Clemens was masterful in his Toronto debut, tossing a six-hitter and striking out nine as the Blue Jays beat the Chicago White Sox 6-1 on Wednesday.

Clemens, pitching his first game for a team other than the Red Sox after 13 seasons as Boston's ace hurler, gave up just one run in the second, walked one and allowed only three runners past second base.

"I'm glad to get that one out of the way, finally," said Clemens, who signed with Toronto as a free agent in the off-season. "It has been a long time coming, at least eight weeks worth of thinking about this night."
White Sox starter Wilson Alvarez was tagged by Benito Santiago's two-run homer in the fourth. He surrendered six runs -- five earned -- and seven hits in 6 1/3 innings.
Orlando Merced, another of the Blue Jays' off-season acquisitions, added a three-run double in the seventh.
In Seattle, Tino Martinez homered in his first three at-bats, drove in seven runs and scored five times as the New York Yankees routed the Mariners, 16-2.
Martinez led a 14-hit, 13-walk New York attack. He had four cracks at a record-tying fourth homer, with three of those at-bats coming with the bases loaded.
Mark Whiten, the last major leaguer to hit four homers in a game, and Paul O'Neil had three hits apiece for the Yankees.
Andy Pettitte tossed six strong innings for the Yanks. He allowed two runs and seven hits. Scott Sanders, who gave up all three Martinez homers, took the loss for Seattle.
In Baltimore, Cal Ripken homered and doubled twice to lift the Orioles to a 4-2 victory over the Kansas City Royals in the season opener for both teams.
Ripken, who moved from shortstop to third base, extended his record consecutive games streak to 2,317. He led off the bottom of the fourth with a homer off Kevin Appier.
Eric Davis doubled home the tie-breaking run in the sixth inning for the Orioles.
Jimmy Key, signed from the New York Yankees as a free agent in the off-season, improved to 7-0 in opening day games. He allowed two unearned runs and four hits over six innings.
In Oakland, David Justice's first American League home run, a two-run shot in the seventh inning, put Cleveland ahead to stay and the Indians held on for a 9-7 win over the Athletics.
Justice, acquired in a blockbuster deal with Atlanta last week, hit a 2-2 pitch from Billy Brewer into the right-field bleachers to snap a 6-6 tie.
The Athletics climbed within 8-7, but Jim Thome homered to lead off the ninth for the final margin.
Steve Kline won in his first major-league appearance, retiring both batters he faced in relief of Charles Nagy.
In Minnesota, Marty Cordova's bases-loaded single in the bottom of the ninth inning scored Pat Meares to lift the Twins to a 7-6 victory over the Detroit Tigers.
Rick Aguilera picked up the win, despite allowing Matt Walbeck's leadoff home run in the top of the ninth.
Bobby Higginson had a two-run homer for Detroit.
Detroit took a 5-4 in the top of the eighth, but the Twins regained the lead in their half of the inning on Greg Colbrunn's two-run homer.
In Anaheim, pinch-hitter Troy O'Leary's RBI single in the top of the ninth inning lifted the Boston Red Sox to a 6-5 win over the Anaheim Angels.
Anaheim led 5-2 entering the top of the ninth and brought on closer Troy Percival, who converted 36 of 39 save opportunities last season.
Percival struck out the first two batters before loading the bases. He then walked in two runs to make it 5-4 and hit Rudy Pemberton to force home the tying run.
Pep Harris came on and allowed O'Leary's infield single that scored the winning run.
